neighbours.label: adverbial complement completing a verb idiom: ' tall' in 'walk tall', ' fine' in 'works just fine', ' loose' in 'ran loose'
fire: After the interview she decided to stand up straight and walk tall into the office.
I was worried about the old laptop, but it runs the new software just fine.
When the gate broke, the goats ran loose across the neighbor's garden.
Coaches told the young players to walk tall even after a hard loss.
The cheap charger works just fine with my phone and tablet.
In those days the dogs roamed loose through the village streets.
He learned to hold his head high and walk tall in front of the crowd.
Don't worry about the update, the printer still prints just fine.
quiet: After the interview she decided to stand up and walk quickly into the office.
I was worried about the old laptop, and it struggles to run the new software.
When the gate broke, the goats wandered across the neighbor's garden.
Coaches told the young players to keep training even after a hard loss.
The cheap charger heats up a lot with my phone and tablet.
In those days the dogs slept by the doors along the village streets.
He learned to speak clearly and stay calm in front of the crowd.
Don't worry about the update, the printer needs a new cartridge.
